name: abdominopelvic cavity
cue: division of the anterior (ventral) cavity that houses the abdominal and pelvic viscera

name: anabolism
cue: assembly of more complex molecules from simpler molecules

name: anatomical position
cue: standard reference position used for describing locations and directions on the human body

name: anatomy
cue: science that studies the form and composition of the body’s structures

name: anterior
cue: describes the front or direction toward the front of the body; also referred to as ventral

name: anterior cavity
cue: larger body cavity located anterior to the posterior (dorsal) body cavity; includes the serous membrane-lined pleural cavities for the lungs, pericardial cavity for the heart, and peritoneal cavity for the abdominal and pelvic organs; also referred to as ventral cavity

name: catabolism
cue: breaking down of more complex molecules into simpler molecules

name: caudal
cue: describes a position below or lower than another part of the body proper; near or toward the tail (in humans, the coccyx, or lowest part of the spinal column); also referred to as inferior

name: cell
cue: smallest independently functioning unit of all organisms; in animals, a cell contains cytoplasm, composed of fluid and organelles

name: computed tomography (CT)
cue: medical imaging technique in which a computer-enhanced cross- sectional X-ray image is obtained

name: control center
cue: compares values to their normal range; deviations cause the activation of an effector

name: cranial
cue: describes a position above or higher than another part of the body proper; also referred to as superior

name: cranial cavity
cue: division of the posterior (dorsal) cavity that houses the brain

name: deep
cue: describes a position farther from the surface of the body

name: development
cue: changes an organism goes through during its life

name: differentiation
cue: process by which unspecialized cells become specialized in structure and function

name: distal
cue: describes a position farther from the point of attachment or the trunk of the body

name: dorsal
cue: describes the back or direction toward the back of the body; also referred to as posterior

name: dorsal cavity
cue: posterior body cavity that houses the brain and spinal cord; also referred to the posterior body cavity

name: effector
cue: organ that can cause a change in a value

name: frontal plane
cue: two-dimensional, vertical plane that divides the body or organ into anterior and posterior portions

name: gross anatomy
cue: study of the larger structures of the body, typically with the unaided eye; also referred to macroscopic anatomy

name: growth
cue: process of increasing in size

name: homeostasis
cue: steady state of body systems that living organisms maintain

name: inferior
cue: describes a position below or lower than another part of the body proper; near or toward the tail (in humans, the coccyx, or lowest part of the spinal column); also referred to as caudal

name: lateral
cue: describes the side or direction toward the side of the body

name: magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
cue: medical imaging technique in which a device generates a magnetic field to obtain detailed sectional images of the internal structures of the body

name: medial
cue: describes the middle or direction toward the middle of the body

name: metabolism
cue: sum of all of the body’s chemical reactions

name: microscopic anatomy
cue: study of very small structures of the body using magnification

name: negative feedback
cue: homeostatic mechanism that tends to stabilize an upset in the body’s physiological condition by preventing an excessive response to a stimulus, typically as the stimulus is removed

name: normal range
cue: range of values around the set point that do not cause a reaction by the control center

name: nutrient
cue: chemical obtained from foods and beverages that is critical to human survival

name: oblique plane
cue: two-dimensional, vertical plane that intersects the body at an angle and is not parallel of perpendicular to any of the other three commonly used planes

name: organ
cue: functionally distinct structure composed of two or more types of tissues

name: organ system
cue: group of organs that work together to carry out a particular function

name: organism
cue: living being that has a cellular structure and that can independently perform all physiologic functions necessary for life

name: pericardium
cue: sac that encloses the heart

name: peritoneum
cue: serous membrane that lines the abdominopelvic cavity and covers the organs found there

name: physiology
cue: science that studies the chemistry, biochemistry, and physics of the body’s functions

name: plane
cue: imaginary two-dimensional surface that passes through the body

name: pleura
cue: serous membrane that lines the pleural cavity and covers the lungs

name: positive feedback
cue: mechanism that intensifies a change in the body’s physiological condition in response to a stimulus

name: positron emission tomography (PET)
cue: medical imaging technique in which radiopharmaceuticals are traced to reveal metabolic and physiological functions in tissues

name: posterior
cue: describes the back or direction toward the back of the body; also referred to as dorsal

name: posterior cavity
cue: posterior body cavity that houses the brain and spinal cord; also referred to as dorsal cavity

name: pressure
cue: force exerted by a substance in contact with another substance

name: prone
cue: face down

name: proximal
cue: describes a position nearer to the point of attachment or the trunk of the body

name: regional anatomy
cue: study of the structures that contribute to specific body regions

name: renewal
cue: process by which worn-out cells are replaced

name: reproduction
cue: process by which new organisms are generated

name: responsiveness
cue: ability of an organisms or a system to adjust to changes in conditions

name: sagittal plane
cue: two-dimensional, vertical plane that divides the body or organ into right and left sides

name: section
cue: in anatomy, a single flat surface of a three- dimensional structure that has been cut through

name: sensor
cue: (also, receptor) reports a monitored physiological value to the control center

name: serosa
cue: membrane that covers organs and reduces friction; also referred to as serous membrane

name: serous membrane
cue: membrane that covers organs and reduces friction; also referred to as serosa

name: set point
cue: ideal value for a physiological parameter; the level or small range within which a physiological parameter such as blood pressure is stable and optimally healthful, that is, within its parameters of homeostasis

name: spinal cavity
cue: division of the dorsal cavity that houses the spinal cord; also referred to as vertebral cavity

name: superficial
cue: describes a position nearer to the surface of the body

name: superior
cue: describes a position above or higher than another part of the body proper; also referred to as cranial

name: supine
cue: face up

name: systemic anatomy
cue: study of the structures that contribute to specific body systems

name: thoracic cavity
cue: division of the anterior (ventral) cavity that houses the heart, lungs, esophagus, and trachea

name: tissue
cue: group of similar or closely related cells that act together to perform a specific function

name: transverse plane
cue: two-dimensional, horizontal plane that divides the body or organ into superior and inferior portions

name: ultrasonography
cue: application of ultrasonic waves to visualize subcutaneous body structures such as tendons and organs

name: ventral
cue: describes the front or direction toward the front of the body; also referred to as anterior

name: ventral cavity
cue: larger body cavity located anterior to the posterior (dorsal) body cavity; includes the serous membrane-lined pleural cavities for the lungs, pericardial cavity for the heart, and peritoneal cavity for the abdominal and pelvic organs; also referred to as anterior body cavity

name: X-ray
cue: form of high energy electromagnetic radiation with a short wavelength capable of penetrating solids and ionizing gases; used in medicine as a diagnostic aid to visualize body structures such as bones

name: acid
cue: compound that releases hydrogen ions (H+) in solution

name: activation energy
cue: amount of energy greater than the energy contained in the reactants, which must be overcome for a reaction to proceed

name: adenosine triphosphate (ATP)
cue: nucleotide containing ribose and an adenine base that is essential in energy transfer

name: amino acid
cue: building block of proteins; characterized by an amino and carboxyl functional groups and a variable side-chain

name: anion
cue: atom with a negative charge

name: atom
cue: smallest unit of an element that retains the unique properties of that element

name: atomic number
cue: number of protons in the nucleus of an atom

name: base
cue: compound that accepts hydrogen ions (H+) in solution

name: bond
cue: electrical force linking atoms

name: buffer
cue: solution containing a weak acid or a weak base that opposes wide fluctuations in the pH of body fluids

name: carbohydrate
cue: class of organic compounds built from sugars, molecules containing carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen in a 1-2-1 ratio

name: catalyst
cue: substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction without itself being changed in the process

name: cation
cue: atom with a positive charge

name: chemical energy
cue: form of energy that is absorbed as chemical bonds form, stored as they are maintained, and released as they are broken

name: colloid
cue: liquid mixture in which the solute particles consist of clumps of molecules large enough to scatter light

name: compound
cue: substance composed of two or more different elements joined by chemical bonds

name: concentration
cue: number of particles within a given space

name: covalent bond
cue: chemical bond in which two atoms share electrons, thereby completing their valence shells

name: decomposition reaction
cue: type of catabolic reaction in which one or more bonds within a larger molecule are broken, resulting in the release of smaller molecules or atoms

name: denaturation
cue: change in the structure of a molecule through physical or chemical means

name: deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA)
cue: deoxyribose-containing nucleotide that stores genetic information

name: disaccharide
cue: pair of carbohydrate monomers bonded by dehydration synthesis via a glycosidic bond

name: disulfide bond
cue: covalent bond formed within a polypeptide between sulfide groups of sulfur- containing amino acids, for example, cysteine

name: electron
cue: subatomic particle having a negative charge and nearly no mass; found orbiting the atom’s nucleus

name: electron shell
cue: area of space a given distance from an atom’s nucleus in which electrons are grouped

name: element
cue: substance that cannot be created or broken down by ordinary chemical means

name: enzyme
cue: protein or RNA that catalyzes chemical reactions

name: exchange reaction
cue: type of chemical reaction in which bonds are both formed and broken, resulting in the transfer of components

name: functional group
cue: group of atoms linked by strong covalent bonds that tends to behave as a distinct unit in chemical reactions with other atoms

name: hydrogen bond
cue: dipole-dipole bond in which a hydrogen atom covalently bonded to an electronegative atom is weakly attracted to a second electronegative atom

name: inorganic compound
cue: substance that does not contain both carbon and hydrogen

name: ion
cue: atom with an overall positive or negative charge

name: ionic bond
cue: attraction between an anion and a cation

name: isotope
cue: one of the variations of an element in which the number of neutrons differ from each other

name: kinetic energy
cue: energy that matter possesses because of its motion

name: lipid
cue: class of nonpolar organic compounds built from hydrocarbons and distinguished by the fact that they are not soluble in water

name: macromolecule
cue: large molecule formed by covalent bonding

name: mass number
cue: sum of the number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus of an atom

name: matter
cue: physical substance; that which occupies space and has mass

name: molecule
cue: two or more atoms covalently bonded together

name: monosaccharide
cue: monomer of carbohydrate; also known as a simple sugar

name: neutron
cue: heavy subatomic particle having no electrical charge and found in the atom’s nucleus

name: nucleotide
cue: class of organic compounds composed of one or more phosphate groups, a pentose sugar, and a base

name: organic compound
cue: substance that contains both carbon and hydrogen

name: peptide bond
cue: covalent bond formed by dehydration synthesis between two amino acids

name: periodic table of the elements
cue: arrangement of the elements in a table according to their atomic number; elements having similar properties because of their electron arrangements compose columns in the table, while elements having the same number of valence shells compose rows in the table

name: pH
cue: negative base-10 logarithm of hydrogen-ion activity, often estimated using hydrogen-ion concentration in dilute solutions

name: phospholipid
cue: a lipid compound in which a phosphate group is combined with a diglyceride

name: phosphorylation
cue: addition of one or more phosphate groups to an organic compound

name: polar molecule
cue: molecule with regions that have opposite charges resulting from uneven numbers of electrons in the nuclei of the atoms participating in the covalent bond

name: polysaccharide
cue: compound consisting of more than two carbohydrate monomers bonded by dehydration synthesis via glycosidic bonds

name: potential energy
cue: stored energy matter possesses because of the positioning or structure of its components

name: product
cue: one or more substances produced by a chemical reaction

name: prostaglandin
cue: lipid compound derived from fatty acid chains and important in regulating several body processes

name: protein
cue: class of organic compounds that are composed of many amino acids linked together by peptide bonds

name: proton
cue: heavy subatomic particle having a positive charge and found in the atom’s nucleus

name: purine
cue: nitrogen-containing base with a double ring structure; adenine and guanine

name: pyrimidine
cue: nitrogen-containing base with a single ring structure; cytosine, thiamine, and uracil

name: radioactive isotope
cue: unstable, heavy isotope that gives off subatomic particles, or electromagnetic energy, as it decays; also called radioisotopes

name: reactant
cue: one or more substances that enter into the reaction

name: ribonucleic acid (RNA)
cue: ribose-containing nucleotide that helps manifest the genetic code as protein

name: solution
cue: homogeneous liquid mixture in which a solute is dissolved into molecules within a solvent

name: steroid
cue: (also, sterol) lipid compound composed of four hydrocarbon rings bonded to a variety of other atoms and molecules

name: substrate
cue: reactant in an enzymatic reaction

name: suspension
cue: liquid mixture in which particles distributed in the liquid settle out over time

name: synthesis reaction
cue: type of anabolic reaction in which two or more atoms or molecules bond, resulting in the formation of a larger molecule

name: triglyceride
cue: lipid compound composed of a glycerol molecule bonded with three fatty acid chains

name: valence shell
cue: outermost electron shell of an atom

name: active transport
cue: form of transport across the cell membrane that requires input of cellular energy

name: amphipathic
cue: describes a molecule that exhibits a difference in polarity between its two ends, resulting in a difference in water solubility

name: anaphase
cue: third stage of mitosis (and meiosis), during which sister chromatids separate into two new nuclear regions of a dividing cell

name: anticodon
cue: consecutive sequence of three nucleotides on a tRNA molecule that is complementary to a specific codon on an mRNA molecule

name: autolysis
cue: breakdown of cells by their own enzymatic action

name: autophagy
cue: lysosomal breakdown of a cell’s own components

name: cell cycle
cue: life cycle of a single cell, from its birth until its division into two new daughter cells

name: cell membrane
cue: membrane surrounding all animal cells, composed of a lipid bilayer interspersed with various molecules; also known as plasma membrane

name: centriole
cue: small, self-replicating organelle that provides the origin for microtubule growth and moves DNA during cell division

name: centromere
cue: region of attachment for two sister chromatids

name: centrosome
cue: cellular structure that organizes microtubules during cell division

name: channel protein
cue: membrane-spanning protein that has an inner pore which allows the passage of one or more substances

name: checkpoint
cue: progress point in the cell cycle during which certain conditions must be met in order for the cell to proceed to a subsequence phase

name: chromatin
cue: substance consisting of DNA and associated proteins

name: chromosome
cue: condensed version of chromatin

name: cilia
cue: small appendage on certain cells formed by microtubules and modified for movement of materials across the cellular surface

name: cleavage furrow
cue: contractile ring that forms around a cell during cytokinesis that pinches the cell into two halves

name: codon
cue: consecutive sequence of three nucleotides on an mRNA molecule that corresponds to a specific amino acid

name: concentration gradient
cue: difference in the concentration of a substance between two regions

name: cyclin
cue: one of a group of proteins that function in the progression of the cell cycle

name: cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK)
cue: one of a group of enzymes associated with cyclins that help them perform their functions

name: cytokinesis
cue: final stage in cell division, where the cytoplasm divides to form two separate daughter cells

name: cytoplasm
cue: internal material between the cell membrane and nucleus of a cell, mainly consisting of a water-based fluid called cytosol, within which are all the other organelles and cellular solute and suspended materials

name: cytoskeleton
cue: “skeleton” of a cell; formed by rod-like proteins that support the cell’s shape and provide, among other functions, locomotive abilities

name: cytosol
cue: clear, semi-fluid medium of the cytoplasm, made up mostly of water

name: diffusion
cue: movement of a substance from an area of higher concentration to one of lower concentration

name: diploid
cue: condition marked by the presence of a double complement of genetic material (two sets of chromosomes, one set inherited from each of two parents)

name: DNA polymerase
cue: enzyme that functions in adding new nucleotides to a growing strand of DNA during DNA replication

name: DNA replication
cue: process of duplicating a molecule of DNA

name: electrical gradient
cue: difference in the electrical charge (potential) between two regions

name: endocytosis
cue: import of material into the cell by formation of a membrane-bound vesicle

name: endoplasmic reticulum (ER)
cue: cellular organelle that consists of interconnected membrane-bound tubules, which may or may not be associated with ribosomes (rough type or smooth type, respectively)

name: exocytosis
cue: export of a substance out of a cell by formation of a membrane-bound vesicle

name: exon
cue: one of the coding regions of an mRNA molecule that remain after splicing

name: extracellular fluid (ECF)
cue: fluid exterior to cells; includes the interstitial fluid, blood plasma, and fluid found in other reservoirs in the body

name: facilitated diffusion
cue: diffusion of a substance with the aid of a membrane protein

name: flagellum
cue: appendage on certain cells formed by microtubules and modified for movement

name: G0 phase
cue: phase of the cell cycle, usually entered from the G1 phase; characterized by long or permanent periods where the cell does not move forward into the DNA synthesis phase

name: G1 phase
cue: first phase of the cell cycle, after a new cell is born

name: G2 phase
cue: third phase of the cell cycle, after the DNA synthesis phase

name: gene
cue: DNA sequence whose expression yields a functional RNA or protein product

name: gene expression
cue: active interpretation of the information coded in a gene to produce a functional gene product

name: genome
cue: entire complement of an organism’s DNA; found within virtually every cell

name: glycocalyx
cue: coating of sugar molecules that surrounds the cell membrane

name: glycoprotein
cue: protein that has one or more carbohydrates attached

name: Golgi apparatus
cue: cellular organelle formed by a series of flattened, membrane-bound sacs that functions in protein modification, tagging, packaging, and transport

name: helicase
cue: enzyme that functions to separate the two DNA strands of a double helix during DNA replication

name: histone
cue: family of proteins that associate with DNA in the nucleus to form chromatin

name: homologous
cue: describes two copies of the same chromosome (not identical), one inherited from each parent

name: hydrophilic
cue: describes a substance or structure attracted to water

name: hydrophobic
cue: describes a substance or structure repelled by water

name: hypertonic
cue: describes a solution concentration that is higher than a reference concentration

name: hypotonic
cue: describes a solution concentration that is lower than a reference concentration

name: integral protein
cue: membrane-associated protein that spans the entire width of the lipid bilayer

name: intermediate filament
cue: type of cytoskeletal filament made of keratin, characterized by an intermediate thickness, and playing a role in resisting cellular tension

name: interphase
cue: entire life cycle of a cell, excluding mitosis

name: interstitial fluid (IF)
cue: fluid in the small spaces between cells not contained within blood vessels

name: intracellular fluid (ICF)
cue: fluid in the cytosol of cells

name: intron
cue: non-coding regions of a pre-mRNA transcript that may be removed during splicing

name: isotonic
cue: describes a solution concentration that is the same as a reference concentration

name: kinetochore
cue: region of a centromere where microtubules attach to a pair of sister chromatids

name: ligand
cue: molecule that binds with specificity to a specific receptor molecule

name: lysosome
cue: membrane-bound cellular organelle originating from the Golgi apparatus and containing digestive enzymes

name: messenger RNA (mRNA)
cue: nucleotide molecule that serves as an intermediate in the genetic code between DNA and protein

name: metaphase
cue: second stage of mitosis (and meiosis), characterized by the linear alignment of sister chromatids in the center of the cell

name: metaphase plate
cue: linear alignment of sister chromatids in the center of the cell, which takes place during metaphase

name: microfilament
cue: the thinnest of the cytoskeletal filaments; composed of actin subunits that function in muscle contraction and cellular structural support

name: microtubule
cue: the thickest of the cytoskeletal filaments, composed of tubulin subunits that function in cellular movement and structural support

name: mitochondrion
cue: one of the cellular organelles bound by a double lipid bilayer that function primarily in the production of cellular energy (ATP)

name: mitosis
cue: division of genetic material, during which the cell nucleus breaks down and two new, fully functional, nuclei are formed

name: mitotic phase
cue: phase of the cell cycle in which a cell undergoes mitosis

name: mitotic spindle
cue: network of microtubules, originating from centrioles, that arranges and pulls apart chromosomes during mitosis

name: multipotent
cue: describes the condition of being able to differentiate into different types of cells within a given cell lineage or small number of lineages, such as a red blood cell or white blood cell

name: mutation
cue: change in the nucleotide sequence in a gene within a cell’s DNA

name: nuclear envelope
cue: membrane that surrounds the nucleus; consisting of a double lipid-bilayer

name: nuclear pore
cue: one of the small, protein-lined openings found scattered throughout the nuclear envelope

name: nucleolus
cue: small region of the nucleus that functions in ribosome synthesis

name: nucleosome
cue: unit of chromatin consisting of a DNA strand wrapped around histone proteins

name: nucleus
cue: cell’s central organelle; contains the cell’s DNA

name: oligopotent
cue: describes the condition of being more specialized than multipotency; the condition of being able to differentiate into one of a few possible cell types

name: organelle
cue: any of several different types of membrane-enclosed specialized structures in the cell that perform specific functions for the cell

name: osmosis
cue: net movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane toward the side with lower water potential

name: passive transport
cue: form of transport across the cell membrane that does not require input of cellular energy

name: peripheral protein
cue: membrane-associated protein that does not span the width of the lipid bilayer, but is attached peripherally to integral proteins, membrane lipids, or other components of the membrane

name: peroxisome
cue: membrane-bound organelle that contains enzymes primarily responsible for detoxifying harmful substances

name: phagocytosis
cue: endocytosis of large particles

name: pinocytosis
cue: endocytosis of fluid

name: pluripotent
cue: describes the condition of being able to differentiate into a large variety of cell types

name: polypeptide
cue: chain of amino acids linked by peptide bonds

name: polyribosome
cue: simultaneous translation of a single mRNA transcript by multiple ribosomes

name: promoter
cue: region of DNA that signals transcription to begin at that site within the gene

name: prophase
cue: first stage of mitosis (and meiosis), characterized by breakdown of the nuclear envelope and condensing of the chromatin to form chromosomes

name: proteome
cue: full complement of proteins produced by a cell (determined by the cell’s specific gene expression)

name: reactive oxygen species (ROS)
cue: a group of extremely reactive peroxides and oxygen-containing radicals that may contribute to cellular damage

name: receptor
cue: protein molecule that contains a binding site for another specific molecule (called a ligand)

name: receptor-mediated endocytosis
cue: endocytosis of ligands attached to membrane-bound receptors

name: ribosomal RNA (rRNA)
cue: RNA that makes up the subunits of a ribosome

name: ribosome
cue: cellular organelle that functions in protein synthesis

name: RNA polymerase
cue: enzyme that unwinds DNA and then adds new nucleotides to a growing strand of RNA for the transcription phase of protein synthesis

name: S phase
cue: stage of the cell cycle during which DNA replication occurs

name: selective permeability
cue: feature of any barrier that allows certain substances to cross but excludes others

name: sister chromatid
cue: one of a pair of identical chromosomes, formed during DNA replication

name: sodium-potassium pump
cue: (also, Na+/K+ ATP-ase) membrane-embedded protein pump that uses ATP to move Na+ out of a cell and K+ into the cell

name: somatic cell
cue: all cells of the body excluding gamete cells

name: spliceosome
cue: complex of enzymes that serves to splice out the introns of a pre-mRNA transcript

name: splicing
cue: the process of modifying a pre-mRNA transcript by removing certain, typically non-coding, regions

name: stem cell
cue: cell that is oligo-, multi-, or pleuripotent that has the ability to produce additional stem cells rather than becoming further specialized

name: telophase
cue: final stage of mitosis (and meiosis), preceding cytokinesis, characterized by the formation of two new daughter nuclei

name: totipotent
cue: embryonic cells that have the ability to differentiate into any type of cell and organ in the body

name: transcription
cue: process of producing an mRNA molecule that is complementary to a particular gene of DNA

name: transcription factor
cue: one of the proteins that regulate the transcription of genes

name: transfer RNA (tRNA)
cue: molecules of RNA that serve to bring amino acids to a growing polypeptide strand and properly place them into the sequence

name: translation
cue: process of producing a protein from the nucleotide sequence code of an mRNA transcript

name: triplet
cue: consecutive sequence of three nucleotides on a DNA molecule that, when transcribed into an mRNA codon, corresponds to a particular amino acid

name: unipotent
cue: describes the condition of being committed to a single specialized cell type

name: vesicle
cue: membrane-bound structure that contains materials within or outside of the cell

name: adipocytes
cue: lipid storage cells

name: adipose tissue
cue: specialized areolar tissue rich in stored fat

name: anchoring junction
cue: mechanically attaches adjacent cells to each other or to the basement membrane

name: apical
cue: that part of a cell or tissue which, in general, faces an open space

name: apocrine secretion
cue: release of a substance along with the apical portion of the cell

name: apoptosis
cue: programmed cell death

name: areolar tissue
cue: (also, loose connective tissue) a type of connective tissue proper that shows little specialization with cells dispersed in the matrix

name: astrocyte
cue: star-shaped cell in the central nervous system that regulates ions and uptake and/or breakdown of some neurotransmitters and contributes to the formation of the blood-brain barrier

name: atrophy
cue: loss of mass and function

name: basal lamina
cue: thin extracellular layer that lies underneath epithelial cells and separates them from other tissues

name: basement membrane
cue: in epithelial tissue, a thin layer of fibrous material that anchors the epithelial tissue to the underlying connective tissue; made up of the basal lamina and reticular lamina

name: cardiac muscle
cue: heart muscle, under involuntary control, composed of striated cells that attach to form fibers, each cell contains a single nucleus, contracts autonomously

name: cell junction
cue: point of cell-to-cell contact that connects one cell to another in a tissue

name: chondrocytes
cue: cells of the cartilage

name: clotting
cue: also called coagulation; complex process by which blood components form a plug to stop bleeding

name: collagen fiber
cue: flexible fibrous proteins that give connective tissue tensile strength

name: connective tissue
cue: type of tissue that serves to hold in place, connect, and integrate the body’s organs and systems

name: connective tissue membrane
cue: connective tissue that encapsulates organs and lines movable joints

name: connective tissue proper
cue: connective tissue containing a viscous matrix, fibers, and cells.

name: cutaneous membrane
cue: skin; epithelial tissue made up of a stratified squamous epithelial cells that cover the outside of the body

name: dense connective tissue
cue: connective tissue proper that contains many fibers that provide both elasticity and protection

name: ectoderm
cue: outermost embryonic germ layer from which the epidermis and the nervous tissue derive

name: elastic cartilage
cue: type of cartilage, with elastin as the major protein, characterized by rigid support as well as elasticity

name: elastic fiber
cue: fibrous protein within connective tissue that contains a high percentage of the protein elastin that allows the fibers to stretch and return to original size

name: endocrine gland
cue: groups of cells that release chemical signals into the intercellular fluid to be picked up and transported to their target organs by blood

name: endoderm
cue: innermost embryonic germ layer from which most of the digestive system and lower respiratory system derive

name: endothelium
cue: tissue that lines vessels of the lymphatic and cardiovascular system, made up of a simple squamous epithelium

name: epithelial membrane
cue: epithelium attached to a layer of connective tissue

name: epithelial tissue
cue: type of tissue that serves primarily as a covering or lining of body parts, protecting the body; it also functions in absorption, transport, and secretion

name: exocrine gland
cue: group of epithelial cells that secrete substances through ducts that open to the skin or to internal body surfaces that lead to the exterior of the body

name: fibroblast
cue: most abundant cell type in connective tissue, secretes protein fibers and matrix into the extracellular space

name: fibrocartilage
cue: tough form of cartilage, made of thick bundles of collagen fibers embedded in chondroitin sulfate ground substance

name: fibrocyte
cue: less active form of fibroblast

name: fluid connective tissue
cue: specialized cells that circulate in a watery fluid containing salts, nutrients, and dissolved proteins

name: gap junction
cue: allows cytoplasmic communications to occur between cells

name: goblet cell
cue: unicellular gland found in columnar epithelium that secretes mucous

name: ground substance
cue: fluid or semi-fluid portion of the matrix

name: histamine
cue: chemical compound released by mast cells in response to injury that causes vasodilation and endothelium permeability

name: histology
cue: microscopic study of tissue architecture, organization, and function

name: holocrine secretion
cue: release of a substance caused by the rupture of a gland cell, which becomes part of the secretion

name: hyaline cartilage
cue: most common type of cartilage, smooth and made of short collagen fibers embedded in a chondroitin sulfate ground substance

name: inflammation
cue: response of tissue to injury

name: lacunae
cue: (singular = lacuna) small spaces in bone or cartilage tissue that cells occupy

name: lamina propria
cue: areolar connective tissue underlying a mucous membrane

name: loose connective tissue
cue: (also, areolar tissue) type of connective tissue proper that shows little specialization with cells dispersed in the matrix

name: matrix
cue: extracellular material which is produced by the cells embedded in it, containing ground substance and fibers

name: merocrine secretion
cue: release of a substance from a gland via exocytosis

name: mesenchymal cell
cue: adult stem cell from which most connective tissue cells are derived

name: mesenchyme
cue: embryonic tissue from which connective tissue cells derive

name: mesoderm
cue: middle embryonic germ layer from which connective tissue, muscle tissue, and some epithelial tissue derive

name: mesothelium
cue: simple squamous epithelial tissue which covers the major body cavities and is the epithelial portion of serous membranes

name: mucous connective tissue
cue: specialized loose connective tissue present in the umbilical cord

name: mucous gland
cue: group of cells that secrete mucous, a thick, slippery substance that keeps tissues moist and acts as a lubricant

name: mucous membrane
cue: tissue membrane that is covered by protective mucous and lines tissue exposed to the outside environment

name: muscle tissue
cue: type of tissue that is capable of contracting and generating tension in response to stimulation; produces movement.

name: myelin
cue: layer of lipid inside some neuroglial cells that wraps around the axons of some neurons

name: myocyte
cue: muscle cells

name: necrosis
cue: accidental death of cells and tissues

name: nervous tissue
cue: type of tissue that is capable of sending and receiving impulses through electrochemical signals.

name: neuroglia
cue: supportive neural cells

name: neuron
cue: excitable neural cell that transfer nerve impulses

name: oligodendrocyte
cue: neuroglial cell that produces myelin in the brain

name: parenchyma
cue: functional cells of a gland or organ, in contrast with the supportive or connective tissue of a gland or organ

name: primary union
cue: condition of a wound where the wound edges are close enough to be brought together and fastened if necessary, allowing quicker and more thorough healing

name: pseudostratified columnar epithelium
cue: tissue that consists of a single layer of irregularly shaped and sized cells that give the appearance of multiple layers; found in ducts of certain glands and the upper respiratory tract

name: reticular fiber
cue: fine fibrous protein, made of collagen subunits, which cross-link to form supporting “nets” within connective tissue

name: reticular lamina
cue: matrix containing collagen and elastin secreted by connective tissue; a component of the basement membrane

name: reticular tissue
cue: type of loose connective tissue that provides a supportive framework to soft organs, such as lymphatic tissue, spleen, and the liver

name: Schwann cell
cue: neuroglial cell that produces myelin in the peripheral nervous system

name: secondary union
cue: wound healing facilitated by wound contraction

name: serous gland
cue: group of cells within the serous membrane that secrete a lubricating substance onto the surface

name: serous membrane
cue: type of tissue membrane that lines body cavities and lubricates them with serous fluid

name: simple columnar epithelium
cue: tissue that consists of a single layer of column-like cells; promotes secretion and absorption in tissues and organs

name: simple cuboidal epithelium
cue: tissue that consists of a single layer of cube-shaped cells; promotes secretion and absorption in ducts and tubules

name: simple squamous epithelium
cue: tissue that consists of a single layer of flat scale-like cells; promotes diffusion and filtration across surface

name: skeletal muscle
cue: usually attached to bone, under voluntary control, each cell is a fiber that is multinucleated and striated

name: smooth muscle
cue: under involuntary control, moves internal organs, cells contain a single nucleus, are spindle-shaped, and do not appear striated; each cell is a fiber

name: stratified columnar epithelium
cue: tissue that consists of two or more layers of column-like cells, contains glands and is found in some ducts

name: stratified cuboidal epithelium
cue: tissue that consists of two or more layers of cube-shaped cells, found in some ducts

name: stratified squamous epithelium
cue: tissue that consists of multiple layers of cells with the most apical being flat scale-like cells; protects surfaces from abrasion

name: striation
cue: alignment of parallel actin and myosin filaments which form a banded pattern

name: supportive connective tissue
cue: type of connective tissue that provides strength to the body and protects soft tissue

name: synovial membrane
cue: connective tissue membrane that lines the cavities of freely movable joints, producing synovial fluid for lubrication

name: tight junction
cue: forms an impermeable barrier between cells

name: tissue
cue: group of cells that are similar in form and perform related functions

name: tissue membrane
cue: thin layer or sheet of cells that covers the outside of the body, organs, and internal cavities

name: totipotent
cue: embryonic cells that have the ability to differentiate into any type of cell and organ in the body

name: transitional epithelium
cue: form of stratified epithelium found in the urinary tract, characterized by an apical layer of cells that change shape in response to the presence of urine

name: vasodilation
cue: widening of blood vessels

name: wound contraction
cue: process whereby the borders of a wound are physically drawn together

name: acne
cue: inflammatory disorder of hair follicles and sebaceous glands involving plugging, sebum and microbial activity

name: albinism
cue: group of inherited conditions that reduce melanin production or distribution in the skin, hair or eyes

name: anagen
cue: active phase of the hair growth cycle

name: apocrine sweat gland
cue: type of sweat gland that is associated with hair follicles in the armpits and genital regions

name: arrector pili
cue: smooth muscle that is activated in response to external stimuli that pull on hair follicles and make the hair “stand up”

name: basal cell
cue: type of stem cell found in the stratum basale and in the hair matrix that continually undergoes cell division, producing the keratinocytes of the epidermis

name: basal cell carcinoma
cue: cancer that originates from basal cells in the epidermis of the skin

name: bedsore
cue: sore on the skin that develops when regions of the body start necrotizing due to constant pressure and lack of blood supply; also called decubitus ulcers

name: callus
cue: thickened area of skin that arises due to constant abrasion

name: catagen
cue: transitional phase marking the end of the anagen phase of the hair growth cycle

name: corn
cue: type of callus that is named for its shape and the elliptical motion of the abrasive force

name: cortex
cue: in hair, the second or middle layer of keratinocytes originating from the hair matrix, as seen in a cross-section of the hair bulb

name: cuticle
cue: in hair, the outermost layer of keratinocytes originating from the hair matrix, as seen in a cross- section of the hair bulb

name: dermal papilla
cue: (plural = dermal papillae) extension of the papillary layer of the dermis that increases surface contact between the epidermis and dermis

name: dermis
cue: layer of skin between the epidermis and hypodermis, composed mainly of connective tissue and containing blood vessels, hair follicles, sweat glands, and other structures

name: desmosome
cue: structure that forms an impermeable junction between cells

name: eccrine sweat gland
cue: type of sweat gland that is common throughout the skin surface; it produces a hypotonic sweat for thermoregulation

name: eczema
cue: skin condition due to an allergic reaction, which resembles a rash

name: elastin fibers
cue: fibers made of the protein elastin that increase the elasticity of the dermis

name: eleiden
cue: clear protein-bound lipid found in the stratum lucidum that is derived from keratohyalin and helps to prevent water loss

name: epidermis
cue: outermost tissue layer of the skin

name: eponychium
cue: nail fold that meets the proximal end of the nail body, also called the cuticle

name: external root sheath
cue: outer layer of the hair follicle that is an extension of the epidermis, which encloses the hair root

name: first-degree burn
cue: superficial burn that injures only the epidermis

name: fourth-degree burn
cue: burn in which full thickness of the skin and underlying muscle and bone is damaged

name: glassy membrane
cue: the basement membrane that is found between the epithelium of the external root sheath and the connective tissue sheath

name: hair
cue: keratinous filament growing out of the epidermis

name: hair bulb
cue: structure at the base of the hair root that surrounds the dermal papilla

name: hair follicle
cue: cavity or sac from which hair originates

name: hair matrix
cue: layer of basal cells from which a strand of hair grows

name: hair papilla
cue: mass of connective tissue, blood capillaries, and nerve endings at the base of the hair follicle

name: hair root
cue: part of hair that is below the epidermis anchored to the follicle

name: hair shaft
cue: part of hair that is above the epidermis but is not anchored to the follicle

name: hypodermis
cue: connective tissue connecting the integument to the underlying bone and muscle

name: hyponychium
cue: thickened layer of stratum corneum that lies below the free edge of the nail

name: integumentary system
cue: skin and its accessory structures

name: internal root sheath
cue: innermost layer of keratinocytes in the hair follicle that surround the hair root up to the hair shaft

name: keloid
cue: type of scar that has layers raised above the skin surface

name: keratin
cue: type of structural protein that gives skin, hair, and nails its hard, water-resistant properties

name: keratinocyte
cue: cell that produces keratin and is the most predominant type of cell found in the epidermis

name: keratohyalin
cue: granulated protein found in the stratum granulosum

name: Langerhans cell
cue: specialized dendritic cell found in the stratum spinosum that functions as a macrophage

name: lunula
cue: basal part of the nail body that consists of a crescent-shaped layer of thick epithelium

name: medulla
cue: in hair, the innermost layer of keratinocytes originating from the hair matrix

name: Meissner corpuscle
cue: (also, tactile corpuscle) receptor in the skin that responds to light touch

name: melanin
cue: pigment that determines the color of hair and skin

name: melanocyte
cue: cell found in the stratum basale of the epidermis that produces the pigment melanin

name: melanoma
cue: type of skin cancer that originates from the melanocytes of the skin

name: melanosome
cue: intercellular vesicle that transfers melanin from melanocytes into keratinocytes of the epidermis

name: Merkel cell
cue: receptor cell in the stratum basale of the epidermis that responds to the sense of touch

name: metastasis
cue: spread of cancer cells from a source to other parts of the body

name: nail bed
cue: layer of epidermis upon which the nail body forms

name: nail body
cue: main keratinous plate that forms the nail

name: nail cuticle
cue: fold of epithelium that extends over the nail bed, also called the eponychium

name: nail fold
cue: fold of epithelium at that extend over the sides of the nail body, holding it in place

name: nail root
cue: part of the nail that is lodged deep in the epidermis from which the nail grows

name: Pacinian corpuscle
cue: (also, lamellated corpuscle) receptor in the skin that responds to vibration

name: papillary layer
cue: superficial layer of the dermis, made of loose, areolar connective tissue

name: reticular layer
cue: deeper layer of the dermis; it has a reticulated appearance due to the presence of abundant collagen and elastin fibers

name: rickets
cue: disease in children caused by vitamin D deficiency, which leads to the weakening of bones

name: scar
cue: collagen-rich skin formed after the process of wound healing that is different from normal skin

name: sebaceous gland
cue: type of oil gland found in the dermis all over the body and helps to lubricate and waterproof the skin and hair by secreting sebum

name: sebum
cue: oily substance that is composed of a mixture of lipids that lubricates the skin and hair

name: second-degree burn
cue: partial-thickness burn that injures the epidermis and a portion of the dermis

name: squamous cell carcinoma
cue: type of skin cancer that originates from the stratum spinosum of the epidermis

name: stratum basale
cue: deepest layer of the epidermis, made of epidermal stem cells

name: stratum corneum
cue: most superficial layer of the epidermis

name: stratum granulosum
cue: layer of the epidermis superficial to the stratum spinosum

name: stratum lucidum
cue: layer of the epidermis between the stratum granulosum and stratum corneum, found only in thick skin covering the palms, soles of the feet, and digits

name: stratum spinosum
cue: layer of the epidermis superficial to the stratum basale, characterized by the presence of desmosomes

name: stretch mark
cue: mark formed on the skin due to a sudden growth spurt and expansion of the dermis beyond its elastic limits

name: sudoriferous gland
cue: sweat gland

name: telogen
cue: resting phase of the hair growth cycle initiated with catagen and terminated by the beginning of a new anagen phase of hair growth

name: third-degree burn
cue: burn that penetrates and destroys the full thickness of the skin (epidermis and dermis)

name: vitamin D
cue: compound that aids absorption of calcium and phosphates in the intestine to improve bone health

name: vitiligo
cue: skin condition in which melanocytes in certain areas lose the ability to produce melanin, possibly due an autoimmune reaction that leads to loss of color in patches
